Current management strategies remain fragmented and reactive, limiting the effectiveness of the One Health paradigm. This review introduces an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered One Health framework designed to transition from surveillance to predictive prevention. Using a literature review across PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, and Web of Science (up to October 2025), recent advances in machine learning, deep learning, geospatial AI, and physics-informed models for chemical risk assessment are synthesized.
